claims.statement: Registering an app in the Asana developer console yields a client ID and a client secret that must be protected like a password; the client secret is sent to the token exchange endpoint from the app server.

sources.supports: Take note of the application's client ID and the client secret (which should be protected as a password).
Your client secret is a secret, and it should never be shared with anyone or added into source code that others could gain access to.

claims.statement: For app components, the secret used to compute the SHA-256 HMAC signature on requests to the app server (header x-asana-request-signature) is the app's client secret.

sources.supports: For both types of requests, the secret used to compute the signature is your app's client secret which can be found in the OAuth tab for the app in the developer console.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.

openQuestions.question: Candidate is not researched beyond existence: the format (prefix, alphabet, length, checksum) is not recorded and has not been researched by research-family.
The documentation states no literal format for a client secret; the example in the OAuth page is a numeric string of unknown provenance and is not recorded here as a format claim.

The client ID is described as uniquely identifying the app and is sent in the browser-visible authorization URL, but the page does not classify its confidentiality. Whether it is a benign public identifier beside this secret is for research-family to establish with a cited statement.

Lead only, not a claim: one scanner rule artifact (gitleaks/gitleaks at b58d3f102cf3a2c84cb7f923d05c25c9b1aed84b, config/gitleaks.toml lines 175-179, read 2026-10-04) uses a 32-character letter-or-digit value near the word "asana" for a client secret, and a 16-digit value for a client ID (lines 169-173). A Semgrep rule set carries ports of the same two rules and counts as the same artifact; the TruffleHog Asana rules describe different shapes and do not corroborate it. tool-corroborated is not met; no structure is recorded.
